Here's the vote result for day 1:

No vote was held today; no one is eliminated.
Night of day 1: player_1 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a vigilante. player_3 was attacked by the serial killer but was saved by the healer!

It's fortunate the healer was active, even if we lost player 1. We know player 3 was targeted by the serial killer. That's our only solid piece of information right now. Since the serial killer acted against player 3, does anyone have thoughts on who might have been trying to make that move?

It's interesting that player_3 was the target of the serial killer. Usually, when someone is targeted by a night killer, they either hold a critical role or are seen as a major threat by the other evil team. Has anyone noticed any inconsistencies in how player_3 has been engaging with us so far? I'm curious if their contributions align with someone genuinely trying to find the wolves, or if there's a reason they caught the serial killer's attention.

It's unsettling to be a target, but I don't see how being targeted by the serial killer reflects on my alignment. If anything, it proves I'm a threat to the killer, not necessarily to the village. I've been trying to stay focused on the game, but I'm open to discussing why you think being targeted implies I'm hiding something.

It is strange that the serial killer keeps going after player_3. Honestly, I'm not sure if that makes them suspicious or just a lucky target. We are still short on solid info, so maybe we should look at who is trying to push the narrative too hard without proof.

It is true that player_3 being targeted repeatedly is suspicious, but we don't have enough proof to act yet. I agree we shouldn't rush into a vote; acting on speculation is exactly what wolves want us to do.

We have abstained twice now, which is exactly what the wolves and the serial killer want, because it guarantees them more nights to kill us off. I know we are short on proof, but we cannot keep stalling while our numbers dwindle. I think it is time we actually evaluate the voting record from yesterday and hold someone accountable, even if it is just to force them to reveal their hand.

I agree with player_7 that we need to stop stalling. It’s frustrating to keep being the SK's target, but focusing only on me won't solve the fact that we have two dead villagers and still no leads. We need to look at who is actually contributing to the group’s progress instead of just repeating that we need to vote.

Stalling is definitely helping the wolves, but voting on pure speculation is dangerous. If we need to move forward, perhaps we should analyze the voting record from yesterday specifically to see who tried to force a target and who avoided it. Let's look at the patterns in the day 2 votes to see if anyone is hiding behind an 'abstain' to stay under the radar.

I agree that abstaining is helping the threats, but just voting to 'break the tie' is how we hit a villager. We should look at player_2, player_4, and myself since we all abstained yesterday. We need to be transparent about why we did that—my reason was lack of info—and see who is just hiding to stay under the radar.

We have spent two days stalling, and while caution is good, it has clearly played into the hands of the wolves. I understand the reluctance to vote without perfect proof, but player 3 has been consistently at the center of the conflict and was the target of a known night-killer. We need to stop theorizing about why we abstain and actually use the voting record we have. Player 3, your defensiveness about the serial killer target is noted, but your insistence that we stop 'stalling' contradicts your behavior when the vote was on the table. Let's focus on the concrete record: player 3 has been protected by the current game state and is drawing the most fire. I suggest we stop the cycle of abstaining and vote on the most suspicious lead we have.

I understand your frustration, player_9, but you're misinterpreting my defense. My 'defensiveness' is just me pointing out that we are burning daylight on a distraction while the actual threats are hiding. If you want to use the voting record, look at who has been consistently pushing for us to remain deadlocked. I'm ready to vote today to break this, are you actually going to propose someone or just keep pointing at the target of the night kills?

We are getting nowhere by just pointing at who the serial killer targeted. If we want to look at the voting record like player_2 suggested, we should focus on the shifts—specifically who might have been trying to steer the 'abstain' movement versus who was actually trying to find a lead. player_9, you are very focused on player_3, but does attacking them actually help us find the wolves, or are we just helping the serial killer narrow their target list by calling out the people they are already tracking?

Player 5, my focus on player 3 isn't just about them being a serial killer target; it's about the fact that they are the most visible node of conflict in this game. We have two dead villagers and zero leads because we keep choosing to abstain rather than evaluate the information we do have. My push for a vote is an attempt to force clarity. I'm not looking to help the serial killer—I'm looking to stop the stalling that is currently letting wolves navigate this game untouched. Let's stop debating why we should vote and actually look at the record; the pattern of constant deadlock is only hurting the village.

We have enough of a record to start looking at patterns instead of just general accusations. Player 2, player 4, and player 8, you all abstained on Day 2. Since that day, you've all correctly identified that inaction helps the wolves. Can you clarify specifically why your read on the board resulted in abstaining rather than picking between the active candidates? If we want to stop the stalling, we need to understand if those votes were truly born from a lack of info or a desire to keep the game in this deadlock.

My vote to abstain was strictly due to the lack of any concrete information to justify an elimination. I didn't want to risk killing a villager on day two when we had almost nothing to go on. Now that we have more discussion, the cost of inaction is clearly higher than the risk of voting, so I'm ready to move past the deadlock and hold someone accountable based on today's contributions.

Player 7, my decision to abstain was born from a genuine lack of evidence. I am against wasting a vote on guesswork when we could easily eliminate a villager and lose an advantage. Now that we have had more discussion, I agree that staying in this deadlock is exactly what the threats want. I'm ready to look at the voting records and analyze who is being consistent and who is just changing their narrative to fit the current momentum.

Player 7, I abstained because I truly lacked enough evidence to justify a vote that could have easily eliminated a villager. I wanted to avoid making a move based solely on speculation, which is risky for our side. However, I agree that our two days of deadlock have now become a liability. Looking at the record, we need to compare who abstained out of caution versus who might be using the cover of a 'no-information' vote to hide their tracks.

I understand the hesitation, but we have to move. Player 3, my suspicion isn't just about the serial killer targeting you—it is about the fact that your contributions are consistently deflecting from our need to act. We have been in a deadlock for two days, and that is a winning state for the wolves. I am proposing we end this stalemate and vote. If you are as frustrated with the stalling as you claim, then join me in proposing an alternative for today's vote so we can finally force someone to be accountable.

Player 9, I hear you, and I agree—the deadlock has to end today. My defensiveness comes from being the target of a witch hunt that ignores the actual game state. If you want a target, look at the players who have been hiding behind 'abstain' votes while we lose villagers. I am fully ready to vote to break this cycle; if you are so concerned about the stall, propose a candidate from the group that has been avoiding the vote, and I will evaluate it with you.

We've spent two full days in a deadlock, and the wolves are the only ones winning in this scenario. Player 2, 4, and 8, you've all acknowledged that stalling is a liability, yet we haven't seen a single attempt to push for a candidate. If you're genuinely ready to move, let's stop talking about 'how' to vote and actually pick a player based on their inconsistency. I'm looking at the record: player 9 was the only one consistently trying to break the cycle, even if their focus on player 3 is narrow. Are we ready to vote for player 9's suggested target, or is there another name we can actually agree on to break this tie?

Player 7, I hear the urgency. While I abstained due to a lack of evidence, the cost of this deadlock is now exceeding the risk of a misvote. If we need to break this, I am ready to look at the voting record again. Player 9 is pushing hard for a vote, which is necessary, but the narrow focus on player 3 feels like it might just be the path of least resistance rather than a genuine search for the wolves. If we are going to act, I want to see a proposal based on something more than just who the serial killer is targeting.

Player 9, your persistence in targeting player 3 feels like it might be a way to force a vote on a convenient target rather than a calculated risk. If we are finally going to break this cycle, we should focus on the voting record. Why not analyze the shifts from day 2 instead of sticking to the same narrow narrative? Let's pick someone whose voting logic or lack thereof is the most inconsistent.

Player 7, I appreciate the push for transparency. My focus on player 3 isn't a narrow fixation, but a direct response to the fact that they are a proven danger. If you want to look at the voting record, we have a clear split: those who enabled two days of stalling and those who tried to push for action. I am ready to vote for player 3 because their defensive deflection has been the most consistent obstacle to our progress. Let's break this stalemate and remove the player who has been hiding in plain sight.

Player 9, you keep framing this as me deflecting, but you're the one fixated on a singular, unproven lead while we're burning time. If we are going to look at the voting record, let's look at the abstainers from Day 2. Players 2, 4, and 8 all claim they abstained out of caution, but that inaction is exactly what got us two dead villagers. If we're voting, we should be looking at who had the most to gain from those abstentions, not just whoever has been under the most pressure.

Since player_3 was a wolf, we really need to look closely at who was consistently trying to push that narrative or conversely, who was trying to deflect from them. Player_4 and player_5, how do you see the remaining field?

It is definitely good we finally removed a wolf. Given the current numbers, we need to be extremely careful. I look at voting records for patterns, and I think we need to look at who specifically enabled the confusion that kept that wolf alive. I have been consistent in my approach because I truly lacked hard data on Day 2 and 3, which is why I abstained earlier, but now that we have a confirmed wolf, I am ready to pressure those who stood by them.

Player 2, I agree we need to be careful. With player 3 gone, the dynamic has shifted significantly. I was actually one of the people who voted to remove player 9 because their fixation on player 3 felt forced, but it turns out they were the investigator, which complicates how I view the previous days' records. I'm focusing on the remaining players to see if anyone is trying to overcompensate now that the heat is on.

The loss of the investigator is a huge blow, especially since they were clearly onto something. Looking back at yesterday's vote, everyone who voted to remove player 9 effectively silenced our best lead. We need to evaluate whether that vote was based on genuine confusion or a coordinated effort by the remaining wolves to protect themselves. I am looking at the record of who pushed hardest for player 9's elimination.

Player 7 makes a good point about the vote against the investigator, but we have to remember that at the time, player 9's narrow focus on player 3 appeared disruptive. It's easy to look back with clarity now that we know player 9's role, but it doesn't necessarily mean everyone who voted for them was a wolf protecting a teammate. We need to look at who is now pushing the hardest to control the narrative today. Player 4, you mentioned looking for patterns in the voting record—what specific patterns in the final day 3 vote stand out to you as most suspicious?

Player 2, the most telling pattern from the Day 3 vote is the divide between those who pushed to remove our investigator, player 9, and those who saw the danger in that. If we look at the final tally, anyone who prioritized removing the investigator over the suspect player 3 effectively cleared the path for the wolves. I am looking closely at the voting history of player 7 and player 5 specifically; we need to decide if that push against player 9 was a genuine mistake or a calculated move to silence the only person with hard data. I think we need to pin down if there was a coordinated attempt to ignore player 9's leads.

Player 4, your logic about the voting record is understandable, but consider that we were all flying blind before the investigator's role was revealed. Targeting players based on a vote that seemed reasonable at the time might distract us from the serial killer who is still active. I think we need to look at who is being unusually opportunistic now that the field has narrowed. Who do you actually suspect, and why?

Player 4, your point about analyzing the vote on player 9 is valid, but we must remember that player 9 was being extremely aggressive, which can look like wolf play to a villager. We need to distinguish between those who voted to remove them because they were suspicious of their behavior and those who voted to silence them. Player 5, what makes you think the serial killer is now the bigger concern than the remaining wolf, and do you have a read on who is acting 'opportunistic'?

Player 7, I focus on the serial killer because they are a rogue element that doesn't follow wolf logic, making them unpredictable and dangerous as our numbers dwindle. I find it suspicious that some are so fixated on re-litigating the Day 3 vote when the real threat is someone who can kill anyone at night. As for being opportunistic, I see those pushing hardest for narrow voting-based conclusions as the ones most likely to be using the chaos to hide their own lack of contribution.

Player 4, I understand your scrutiny of the Day 3 vote, but calling for an analysis of everyone who voted against the investigator overlooks the fact that they were appearing erratic at the time. My concern is that by focusing so heavily on that past vote, we are ignoring the immediate threat of the serial killer who is actively choosing targets every night. If we just chase ghosts from yesterday, we might miss the person making moves right now. Player 5, you mentioned people being opportunistic—who do you think is benefiting most from this current debate?

Player 2, I think those pushing the hardest to re-litigate the past are the ones benefiting most, as it keeps us from looking at who is actually dictating the current flow of the game. It’s convenient to hide behind voting statistics when you don't have to defend your own recent silence or lack of engagement. Right now, anyone trying to turn this into a purely mathematical game is likely the one using that distraction to mask their role.

Player 5, you argue that the serial killer is the bigger threat, but we cannot ignore the remaining wolf who is likely benefiting from the current confusion. My focus on the Day 3 vote isn't to re-litigate the past, but to see if anyone's current push to abandon that evidence is actually a strategy to protect a partner. If you aren't one of them, help me examine who is trying to pivot away from that data the hardest.
